notes: Scope filtered to mechanisms behind the five nominated features. Interventions with no preclinical row and the reason: 131I-apamistamab (Iomab-B) - no primary preclinical anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy paper found for the 131I conjugate itself, so the RIT-conditioning mechanism is carried by the 211At analogue (Orozco 2013); FLAMSA-RIC and second allo-HCT sequencing - no primary preclinical model exists, the evidence base is registry-clinical only; VIP943, BMS-986497/ORM-6151 and CBX-250 have no indexed primary preclinical publication under those designations, though CBX-250's target is covered by the two Alatrash CG1/HLA-A2 papers. Three rows (pre-031 to pre-033) carry intervention_id 'extramedullary-disease-biology', which is not an intervention but the sanctuary-site and antigen-heterogeneity biology that modifies every other option for this patient's thigh myeloid sarcoma; two rows carry 'venetoclax-resistance' on the same basis. Vago 2009 logged considered_excluded because genomic HLA-haplotype loss needs a mismatched haplotype and this graft was HLA-identical sibling.

Horizon scan across the five stated features. Strongest included candidates: CD123-targeted GSPT1 degrader-antibody conjugates (ORM-1153/Hdz-C123A, IND-enabling, p53-independent payload), decitabine + ATR inhibitor as a TP53-selective combination, and multiplex epitope-edited donor graft. Three parent-flagged directions (MECOM/EVI1-CTBP2, del(7q) collateral lethality, del(5q) CK1alpha degraders) were checked and logged considered_excluded because none maps onto a stated targetable_feature; the CK1alpha route is additionally counter-productive because it kills through p53 stabilisation. CD33-deltaE2 excluded on a negative primary result (Godwin 2020 found no surface protein); the C2-set-domain CD33 binder was kept instead. drp1-inhibition-venetoclax-resensitisation rests on a single unreplicated in-vitro paper and is flagged as such in-row. Reference check corrected three conference-abstract author fields from sponsor names to the actual first/last authors via Crossref.

notes: All evidence_citations resolved against trials.jsonl, clinical_evidence.jsonl and preclinical_evidence.jsonl rows in this case directory; no identifier written that does not already appear in the dossier. Preference filter applied per preferences.json: toxicity_vetoes and modality_constraints are both empty so no pick was struck on toxicity or modality grounds; prefers_trials true and geography_band null so trial options were ranked ahead of off-trial ones. Two preference-relevant flags raised rather than silently overridden: (1) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.75 was set before organ function was documented and the free text asks for it to be revisited, which bears most on picks 3 and 4; (2) the stated submission reason, HLA-restricted immunotherapy, is narrowed by prior allo-HCT exclusions on NCT05473910 and NCT06704152 but not closed, since NCT03326921 requires a prior graft and NCT06994676 accepts relapse at any time post-HSCT. WT1-siTCR (HLA-A*24:02) deliberately not ranked despite being named in profile.json, because accessibility.jsonl records no enrolling study reachable from the US.

Rank order mirrors the treatment sequence. Rank 1 is the shared workup because no toxicity claim in this case is anchored without organ-function data; profile.json::organ_function documents none and preferences.json says the 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once fitness is known. Flagged for round 2: Iomab-B cannot be borrowed for this patient (SIERRA and NCT07157514 both exclude prior allo-HCT; NCT07157514 also caps blasts at 20% against ~85%), rezatapopt has no peer-reviewed effect size and needs venetoclax to kill per Carter 2025, and pivekimab carries 2/68 dose-limiting veno-occlusive events which matters ahead of a second conditioning regimen.

Ranked on evidence quality weighted by applicability, which is deliberately not the same ordering as clinical value to this patient. Registry-tier HCT2 platform first (n=2632/399/263/179, replicated prognostic model, ROBINS-I serious throughout, and every favourable stratum blast-gated below 27-35% against her 85%). CLAG-GO second on eligibility fit alone; Hills 2014 (n=3325, RoB2 low) gives adverse cytogenetics OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18, p=0.9) and NCT04050280 has no posted results. HA-1 TCR-T third: n=9 with a feasibility/DLT registered primary endpoint, but construct-specific preclinical (Dossa 2018) plus independent target replication (Pilunov 2023), and the only HA-1 protocol that requires rather than excludes prior allo-HCT. Flagged as evidence errors to avoid: quoting Chapuis 2019 (prophylaxis in remission) for a patient with active post-HCT disease when Mazziotta 2025 is the matching population; treating HA-2 (Heemskerk 2003, in vitro, wrong TCR) as equivalently evidenced to HA-1; citing rezatapopt response rates that exist only as press releases; citing Vadakekolathu 2020's 47% (post-hoc, n=15, no CI); and using CD33 antigen density as a gate for T-cell-redirecting formats when Laszlo 2019 gives r2=0.0136, P=0.45 for that association.

Round-1 position appended to board/positions.jsonl. Ranked cytoreduction (CLAG-GO) ahead of the HLA-restricted immunotherapy the case was submitted for, because 85% marrow blasts gates HA-1 TCR-T, DLI and HCT2 alike. No pick violates preferences.json::toxicity_vetoes (empty).

notes: Round-1 position appended to board/positions.jsonl. Ranked on guideline fit: CLAG-GO on NCT04050280 first because NCCN AML v3.2026 makes clinical trial the strongly preferred R/R route and lists both regimen components separately in the same pathway; HCT2 and DLI next as the cytoreduction-gated consolidation steps; HA-1 TCR-T fourth with the honest note that no guideline lists it, only the trial route it sits in; rezatapopt fifth and contingent on a Y220C call, because NCCN lists clinical trial and nothing else against TP53-mutant/del(17p) poor-risk AML. Version caveat: NCCN appears to have posted 2026 versions later than v3.2026 behind the login, so v3.2026 is the floor I could verify, not necessarily the newest text.

Four cross-critique rows appended in one atomic write. advocate/ha1-tcr-t dissent on the registered feasibility+DLT primary endpoint behind 4 of 9; risktaker/at211-bc8-b10 dissent (chosen over rank 1 because the CLAG-M+Ac225 import is already conceded in their own concerns) on SIERRA's null OS (HR 0.99, 0.70-1.41, p=0.96), declined filing and prior-HCT exclusion, plus a note that Vadakekolathu's 47% (n=15, post-hoc, no CI) should not propagate; conservative/pending-diagnostics-workup qualified, gating logic sound but a workup is not a therapeutic rank; concensusite/second-allo-hct qualified, their no-NCCN-category finding is correct and does not demote HCT2, since what backs it is a replicated prognostic model rather than a replicated treatment effect, with the NCT06616636 Y220C VAF>2% assay-LOD problem noted on their rank 5. No veto issued: nothing in this dossier is retracted or fraud-flagged.

notes: Round-2 critiques appended: qualified on advocate/ha1-tcr-t (route guideline-concordant, rank-1 placement inverts the cytoreduce-first sequence), endorse on conservative/pending-diagnostics-workup (NCCN v3.2026 evaluation already orders HLA typing, chemistries and cardiac assessment; only rs1801284 genotyping is extra-guideline), qualified on critic/second-allo-hct (the widest board-vs-guideline gap: no NCCN category or ELN grade covers a second allograft after post-transplant relapse - uncovered, not contraindicated - and both bodies describe cytoreduction then transplant, against rank 1), qualified on risktaker/clag-go (trial-first matches NCCN listing clinical trial and nothing else for TP53 poor-risk; the CLAG backbone and NCT04050280 population match carry the guideline-fit case, not the gemtuzumab component, which NCCN omits from poor-risk induction and whose registrational trial ALFA-0701 enrolled de novo disease only). Two round-1 flags closed. Menin inhibitor: no persona picked revumenib or any menin inhibitor, so the pre-registered dissent on the KMT2A amplification-vs-rearrangement distinction is moot and closed. Rezatapopt: I withdraw my own rank-5 pick. Critic showed NCT06616636 requires a CLIA Y220C call at VAF above 2%, at the detection limit of the panel that called her TP53-negative, and Carter (pmid 40608889) makes the drug venetoclax-dependent for killing when she has just progressed through venetoclax; conservative and risktaker argued the same way in round 1, and I find the assay-decides-eligibility point decisive. NCCN listing clinical trial and nothing else for TP53-mutated poor-risk AML still stands, and it supports the shape the board converged on - a trial regimen at rank 1 and a trial-hosted cellular option behind cytoreduction - just not that particular trial for this patient absent a variant call. Discipline held: no ESMO-MCBS score quoted anywhere (v1.1 is a solid-tumour scale, not validated for haematological malignancies), and NCCN v3.2026 remains the verified floor, not necessarily the newest text.

The highest-value next action is a records request and a phone call (the ~2020 allele-level HLA report never transcribed into the current chart), plus a blood test on the patient and the sibling donor, run CONCURRENTLY with cycle 1 rather than ahead of it.
